newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil, jet fuel steady.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil, jet fuel steady.

text.p: Singapore physical gas oil prices were steady at firm levels as a local trader continued to provide buying support while jet fuel was well offered at slightly firmer values, traders said on Thursday.
The gas oil market maintained its strength despite a 633,000-barrel build in middle-distillate stocks in Singapore to 5.59 million barrels for the week ending April 9.
This fulfilled market forecast that stocks would rise again after a dramatic draw for the week ending April 2 to 4.95 million barrels, which was at least a three-year low.

The rise in stocks were attributed to arbitrage cargoes which have been offloaded in Singapore, but traders noted that the build was not a large one, indicating that the Singapore trader continued to absorb the incoming cargoes.

With the purchase of two cargoes on Thursday, the Singapore trader and its related firm has so far bought 1.8 million barrels this week, bringing the total to over 11 million barrels since they started buying on March 3.

The trader's sister company on Thursday bought one cargo at $27.10 per barrel for April 25-29 lifting free-on-board (fob) basis, and another at $26.70 for May 6-10 lifting fob, both from a European major, mirroring traded levels seen this week.
"The market is still resilient," one trader said. "People are still expecting the market to go down, but these two buyers are holding it up."

Nevertheless, the weak undertone was reflected on the swaps market with April shaving off 15 cents to be last quoted at $26.45/$26.55 per barrel, while May lost 25 cents to be quoted at $25.35/$25.45.
Traders said the Singapore trader might have already booked most available storage tank space in China for its massive diesel purchases.
Traders said while the sustained strong diesel prices in Asia continued to open the arbitrage window from the west, it was difficult to get vessels to ship the cargoes in.

India was expected to issue its diesel import tender for June arrival either on Friday or early next week. India bought a record 1.5 million tonnes of high speed diesel in 37 cargoes in its tender for June 1996 deliveries. It bought 870,000 tonnes in its previous for May 1997 delivery.

Taiwan will not issue a tender to sell 0.3-percent sulphur diesel for May lifting as it would deliver two term cargoes during that month to a Singapore trader, a CPC source said. But it would soon issue a tender to sell June-lifting cargoes.
Jet fuel was offered by a US trader and a Chinese trader at steady levels--$25.25 per barrel for May 5-9 lifting fob, and $24.75 for May 3-7 lifting.
Swaps jet fuel for balance also relected current steady levels with balance April again traded at $25.00, as was done on Wednesday.
